scope: Read-only sampled power diagnostic from the existing native BC recording; no mj_step, training, source modification, or running-job changes.

method.streaming: 79 NPZ chunks; only current chunk arrays retained, plus 2000 scalar output rows
method.sampling_phase: before-state native indices 79,159,...,159999; times approximately 0.0009875 through 1.9999875 s
method.kinematics: Set saved qpos_before and qvel_before on independent MjData; mj_forward; mj_jacBodyCom gives world linear/angular velocities of each body COM
method.power_formula: sum over bodies of external_body_wrench_native[:3] dot body_COM_world_velocity + external_body_wrench_native[3:] dot body_world_angular_velocity
method.work_formula: rectangle sum(sampled power * 0.001); positive and negative parts integrated separately
method.units: native force*distance per second and native work; absolute SI NOT_ESTABLISHED

force_identity.interpretation: All saved externally applied body wrench in this recording is the declared adhesion; no other applied body wrench or generalized external force detected. Gravity and contact forces are separate and excluded from this power diagnostic.

source_evidence.gate: Any pad positive vertical velocity sets rising=True; loaded legs receive downward adhesion only when not rising. This preferentially applies downward force on downward-moving pads, allowing positive mechanical power rather than a passive symmetric restraint.
source_evidence.refresh: Adhesion refreshed every40 native steps=0.5ms; saved actual wrench is used as applied, already converted to body-COM moment by physics.py. No torque-reference correction was needed in the primary result.
source_evidence.reference_sensitivity: For sensitivity only, additionally translate stored torque from saved adhesion_reference_body_com to current COM: tau+cross(reference_COM-current_COM,F). This changes steady mean power by about0.001767; this is not the primary applied-wrench calculation.

conclusion: The sampled adhesion wrench is strongly net energy-injecting in both settling and steady phases, primarily through translational force power. This supports an energy-pumping mechanism consistent with downward force during descent and release during ascent, and is a concrete candidate contributor to persistent physical oscillation and loaded slip.
limitations: Sampled at a fixed1ms phase; not a full native-rate integral or full energy balance. Actuator work, gravity, contact/friction, damping, stored kinetic/potential energy and numerical dissipation are not balanced here. No adhesion-disabled counterfactual was run, so this does not prove adhesion is the sole cause of slip, nor that biological adhesion or physical walking is impossible. State reconstruction uses the existing model loader and saved states only.
